common_name: Brazos Best Avocado (Cold-Hardy Texas Mexican-Type Avocado)

planting.note: Plant container-grown grafted trees in spring after the danger of frost has passed, in full sun and well-drained soil, and provide young trees with cold protection for their first few winters; Brazos Best is a Texas-selected Mexican-race avocado bred for cold hardiness similar to Joey and Lila.

directions: Plant container-grown grafted trees in spring after the danger of frost has passed, in full sun and well-drained soil, and provide young trees with cold protection for their first few winters. Brazos Best is a Texas-selected Mexican-race avocado prized alongside cultivars like Joey and Lila for cold hardiness well beyond that of standard Guatemalan or West Indian avocado types, allowing it to survive brief hard freezes that would kill most avocado trees. It produces small to medium, thin-skinned, purple-black fruit with rich, nutty-flavored flesh typical of Mexican-race avocados, ripening in late summer through fall. Its combination of cold tolerance and dependable fruiting makes it one of the more practical avocado choices for in-ground planting in the milder parts of the Gulf Coast and coastal Texas, where standard avocado cultivars are too tender.
sources: Texas A&M AgriLife Extension — Avocado Production in Texas
